merger_description:
McCormick & Company, Incorporated (McCormick) proposes to acquire Unilever PLC’s (Unilever) global foods business, excluding Unilever’s food businesses in India, Nepal and Portugal, and Unilever’s Lifestyle and Nutrition, Buavita and Lipton Ready to Drink businesses (Unilever Foods) (the Acquisition).

Unilever will incorporate a new Australian entity, Australia Food NewCo, and transfer Unilever Foods’ Australian business to that entity. On completion, Unilever will transfer 100% of the shares in Australia Food NewCo to a McCormick UK holding company.

McCormick is a US-headquartered, publicly listed global manufacturer, marketer and distributor of spices, herbs, seasoning mixes, sauces, condiments and other flavour-related products. McCormick operates through two business segments: Consumer, through which it supplies products to customers via retail channels, and Flavour Solutions, through which it supplies food service customers and food manufacturers with products and customised flavouring solutions.

Unilever Foods is one of Unilever business groups, and it comprises a portfolio of about 75 brands. Unilever Foods’ business areas can be categorised into condiments (including mayonnaise, ketchup and mustards), cooking aids and mini meals (including soups, bouillons, seasonings, recipe sauces, ready meals and gravy products), and Unilever Food Solutions, through which it provides products and solutions to food service customers.

Unilever is a UK-headquartered, fast-moving consumer goods group listed on the London Stock Exchange and Euronext Amsterdam.

McCormick and Unilever Foods overlap primarily in the retail supply of recipe mixes, side dishes and bottled sauces in Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, third party and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties are not close competitors in the supply of recipe
mixes, side dishes and bottled sauces in Australia.
• In relation to the supply of side dishes, despite concerns raised
in third-party feedback regarding consolidation, McCormick is a
small competitor and the increase in the merged entity’s market
share would be limited.
• In relation to the supply of recipe mixes and bottled sauces, the
aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is estimated to be
low.
• The merged entity would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of recipe mixes, side dishes and
bottled sauces through retail channels in Australia.
